dedupe_keys.name: comando open source python framework for component oriented modelling and nonlinear design and operation optimisation of integrated energy systems

description: COMANDO is an open-source Python package for modelling and optimising the design and operation of integrated energy systems, whose licence names Forschungszentrum Jülich's energy systems engineering institute. The 2021 arXiv paper read on 2026-09-28 explains that system models are assembled from component models that may be nonlinear, dynamic and discrete, and that one system model can be turned into different deterministic or stochastic optimisation problems by changing the objective and data or applying automatic reformulations, with hooks for custom initialisation, decomposition and sequential solution. Its case studies show automated linearisation, dynamic optimisation, stochastic programming and neural network surrogates in global optimisation. The Python package index lists version 1.2.1 of July 2026 under the MIT licence, with source code on Jülich's GitLab and documentation on Read the Docs. Coverage is not geographic: it models any site or district energy system. Access is free under MIT. Caveats: nonlinear problems need external solvers and expertise, and the case studies are illustrative, not validated plants. It supports optimisation and capacity planning studies, such as sizing heat pumps, storage and combined heat and power units for a district energy system under uncertain demand. Related record: EnergyPLAN offers a simpler hourly energy system simulation.
